# Private annex — `<skill>@<sha>`

Delivered to the skill's author only. Never published alongside the public capability report.

This is the optimization half of the work (see
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-30-skills-factory-mvp-design.md` §1.1): the report proves the
number, this annex is how you move it. Manual-first — every finding below is written by a human
who read the transcripts listed in "Evidence", not generated by a model.

Working set: `yarn tsx scripts/skills-bench/list-failing-sessions.ts --run <run-dir> --arm <skill>`
lists every attempt that failed or regressed, with its transcript and session-file paths.

## 2. Findings by failure mode

Every failing/regressed attempt from the working set belongs in exactly one of the three
categories below. Findings with no attempts in a category should say so plainly ("no attempts in
this category") rather than being omitted.

### 2.1 Never triggered

The skill was mounted but the model never invoked it (`triggered: no` in the working set) — a
discoverability problem, not a content problem.

### 2.2 Triggered but vague

The skill loaded, but its guidance was too unspecific for the model to act on (the transcript shows
the model reading the skill, then proceeding as if it hadn't).

### 2.3 Triggered and harmful

(`outcome: regressed` in the working set — the baseline resolved, the treatment did not).

## 4. Re-evaluation offer

If you revise the skill, we will measure the revision on a fresh task set — tasks the diagnosis
above was never derived from (a held-back portion of the original candidates, or a newly authored
set), per spec §3.1 step 7. Diagnosis tasks are burned for this skill's lineage (`<skill>@<sha>`
and its descendants); the re-evaluation runs on tasks that have not seen this annex. A revision
that measurably improves earns the badge; a revision that does not is reported honestly, and the
offer to re-run again stands.

To request re-evaluation, reply with the commit or tag of the revised skill.
